newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas mostly ends up but still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas mostly ends up but still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended higher Friday in lackluster activity, with a firmer cash and forecasts for more heat next week lifting the complex though prices remained in recent ranges.
August climbed 1.6 cents to close at $2.139 per million British thermal units. Sept settled two cents higher at $2.14.

"We couldn't break through the (up) trendline, so the shorts ended up covering before the weekend. We could see a minor rebound with the heat next week, but if the weather doesn't last, we could be in a sell-the-rally mode," said one Midwest trader, adding the seasonal decline may have begun.

Hot, humid weather was expected to dominate the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions next week, giving the bulls some hope that physical prices will be fairly well supported when July flows begin.
But most agreed the bears could quickly take control once temperatures turn more moderate, particularly with inventories in good shape at this point in the injection cycle.

Chart traders noted August held support along the up trendline at $2.105. Next support was seen at the recent $2.08 low. Trendline resistance was seen in the $2.27 area, with further selling likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.
Some technicians noted weekly stochastics were close to crossing to the downside.

In the July cash Friday, Gulf Coast gas firmed slightly to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were steady to off slightly at about $2. New York city gate gas for July was quoted in the mid-$2.40s, up five cents on the day.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip edged up 0.1 cent to $2.209. NYMEX said 26,650 contracts traded, down sharply from Thursday's revised tally of 94,813.
On the KCBT, August finished 1.5 cents higher at $2.015, while deferreds ended up by one-half to one cent. The East/West spread widened by 0.1 cent to 12.4 cents (NYMEX premium).
